title: Float Switch / Long Fill
shortDescription: Water reservoir did not fill within allowed time.
fullDescription: Hoshizaki E1 indicates the float switch did not register the high water level within the fill timer (typically 6 minutes). This stops the freeze cycle to prevent dry running. Causes include closed water supply, scaled or stuck float, clogged inlet screen, or failed inlet valve.

fixSteps.title: Verify supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm water shutoff fully open, replace prefilter if installed.

fixSteps.title: Clean float
fixSteps.instruction: Descale float switch and reservoir per Hoshizaki Cleaning Plus procedure.

fixSteps.title: Test inlet valve
fixSteps.instruction: Apply 120V to coil and verify flow. Replace if no flow with full pressure.

whenToCallPro: If supply, screens, and valve test good, contact a tech for board diagnosis.

faq.q: How often should I clean the float?
faq.a: Every 6 months minimum, more often in hard water.

title: Long Freeze Cycle
shortDescription: Freeze cycle exceeded the maximum time.
fullDescription: E2 sets when the freeze cycle exceeds 60 minutes. The thermistor on the suction line did not reach the freeze setpoint. Cause is typically poor heat rejection, low refrigerant, or thermistor problems.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Deep-clean coil and verify clearances and ambient temps.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance against Hoshizaki temp/resistance chart and replace if out of spec.

fixSteps.title: Refrigeration check
fixSteps.instruction: Certified tech to verify charge, subcooling, and superheat.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant work requires EPA-certified service.

faq.a: Yes, anything reducing condenser performance, including high room temp, can trip E2.

title: Long Harvest Cycle
shortDescription: Harvest cycle did not complete within allowed time.
fullDescription: E3 indicates the harvest cycle exceeded its maximum (typically 20 minutes). The slab is not releasing or the harvest thermistor is not reaching setpoint. Common causes are scale on the evaporator and stuck hot-gas valve.

fixSteps.title: Descale evaporator
fixSteps.instruction: Run Hoshizaki Scale Away cycle following manual.

fixSteps.title: Test hot-gas valve
fixSteps.instruction: Verify coil voltage during harvest and replace coil/valve if no operation.

whenToCallPro: Hot-gas valve replacement involves refrigerant recovery.

faq.a: Often yes, if scale is the root cause. If E3 persists, check hot-gas valve.

title: High Discharge Temperature
shortDescription: Compressor discharge temperature too high.
fullDescription: E4 indicates the discharge thermistor sensed a temperature exceeding safe limits. The control halts the compressor to protect it. Root causes include condenser fouling, fan failure, or low refrigerant.

fixSteps.title: Clean coil
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum and brush condenser, ensuring clear airflow.

fixSteps.title: Test fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify fan runs continuously during freeze. Check capacitor.

whenToCallPro: Persistent E4 after airflow corrections needs refrigeration diagnosis.
videoSearchQuery: Hoshizaki E4 high discharge temp fix

faq.q: Should I just keep resetting it?
faq.a: No. Repeated resets without fixing the cause will damage the compressor.

title: Bin Control Sensor Error
shortDescription: Bin level sensor open, shorted, or out of range.
fullDescription: E5 means the bin thermistor reading is invalid. Without bin level data the unit cannot decide whether to make ice. Most often a wiring issue or a damaged thermistor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check bin sensor connector for damage, corrosion, or pulled pins.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance and compare to chart at known temperature.

whenToCallPro: If thermistor and harness check good, the board may be the issue.

faq.q: Will the unit run with E5?
faq.a: No, the control needs valid bin data to operate safely.

title: High Pressure Switch Activated
shortDescription: High pressure cutout opened, locking out the compressor.
fullDescription: E7 fires after the high-pressure switch trips, often multiple times. Causes include heavily blocked condenser, failed fan, refrigerant overcharge, or non-condensables.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Thorough coil cleaning and clearance check.

fixSteps.title: Refrigeration check
fixSteps.instruction: Tech to verify pressures, switch operation, and charge weight.

whenToCallPro: Refrigeration faults need certified service.

faq.a: On the discharge line near the compressor; consult your unit's service manual.

title: Compressor Over-Current
shortDescription: Compressor amperage exceeded safe limit.
fullDescription: E8 fires when current sensing detects compressor amperage too high. Often a starting issue (failed start capacitor or relay) or a mechanical problem in the compressor itself.

fixSteps.title: Check supply voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Verify voltage at unit within nameplate tolerance.

fixSteps.title: Test start components
fixSteps.instruction: Replace start capacitor and relay if compressor fails to start.

whenToCallPro: Compressor replacement and refrigerant work require certification.

faq.q: How long should a compressor last?
faq.a: 10-15 years with proper maintenance and clean condensers.

title: Pump Motor Fault
shortDescription: Water pump not running or current out of range.
fullDescription: Hoshizaki E9 reports the recirculation pump is not operating correctly. Without proper water flow, ice cubes will be undersized or harvest will fail.

causes.cause: Seized pump impeller from scale or debris

fixSteps.title: Inspect pump
fixSteps.instruction: Remove pump, clean impeller and housing, check shaft rotation.

fixSteps.title: Test motor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance and supply voltage. Replace if motor failed.

whenToCallPro: If a new pump still fails, control board needs evaluation.

faq.q: Can scale really seize a pump?
faq.a: Yes. Heavy mineral deposits cement impellers and bearings if cleaning is skipped.

title: Bin Full Indicator
shortDescription: Bin sensor reports full condition.
fullDescription: When ice level reaches the bin thermistor, Hoshizaki halts the freeze cycle and displays bin full. If no actual ice is present, the thermistor likely reads cold due to a failed sensor or wiring issue.
symptoms: No ice production with empty bin

fixSteps.title: Empty bin
fixSteps.instruction: Clear ice and observe whether unit resumes production.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance at room temp; replace if outside spec.

whenToCallPro: If sensor and wiring check OK, board diagnosis is needed.

faq.a: Sometimes; clear bin first, then power-cycle if needed.

title: Cleaning Indicator
shortDescription: Cleaning interval reached.
fullDescription: Hoshizaki tracks operating time and signals the operator when cleaning is due. The unit continues to run, but cleaning should be scheduled promptly to avoid scale buildup that triggers other faults.

fixSteps.title: Run clean cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Use Scale Away (nickel-safe) per manual procedure.

fixSteps.title: Sanitize
fixSteps.instruction: Run sanitizing cycle after cleaning.

whenToCallPro: Most operators handle cleaning; deeper service is rarely needed.

faq.a: Hoshizaki Scale Away or another nickel-safe ice machine cleaner approved for KM/KMD.

title: Pump Motor Overload
shortDescription: Circulation pump drew excess current.

fixSteps.title: Free impeller
fixSteps.instruction: Pull pump, descale impeller, spin freely.

fixSteps.title: Test capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure capacitance against nameplate value.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: Install new pump assembly and prime.
